terms.gloss: a vow, a solemn promise to a god; later also a wish, a prayer
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.18.1: vōtō et prōmissō tenērī (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 7.40.6: ejus mē compotem vōtī facere vōs potestis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To make a vow: vōtum facere, suscipere; to pay it: vōtum solvere, reddere (Cicero). The sense “wish” is perhaps not older than Augustus’s time (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: to vow, promise solemnly to a god
evidence: Cic. ND 3.88: neque Herculī quisquam decumam vōvit umquam (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 5.21.2: tibi hinc decimam partem praedae voveō (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: vōta puer solvit, quae fēmina vōverat
phrases.english: as a boy he paid the vows he had made as a woman

phrases.latin: tibi hinc decimam partem praedae voveō
phrases.english: I vow you a tenth part of the spoil from here

sources: Lewis & Short: votum · Lewis & Short: voveo
